label: FP
reason: The XSS vulnerability claim is based on a misinterpretation of the code flow. The user-provided header name is filtered out via commonHeaders check and only used if it's not a standard header. Even if a malicious header name were passed, it is never directly rendered in HTML without going through ESAPI encoder().encodeForHTML(), which sanitizes the input. Furthermore, the value is processed via doSomething() where it is safely assigned to bar, and then only used in a cryptographic operation that does not involve direct rendering. There is no unescaped user input being written to HTML output.

evidence.note: Header name extraction with filtering of common headers prevents injection
All user inputs go through ESAPI.encodeForHTML() before being printed, preventing XSS
The input is sanitized using encodeForHTML prior to inclusion in HTML response
